verses.text: So what advantage is there in being a Jew? What value is there in circumcision?
Much in every way! First of all, the Jews were trusted with the very words of God.
What if some of them were unfaithful? Does their unfaithfulness cancel God's faithfulness?
Not at all! Let God be true, even if every human being is a liar. As the Scriptures say, "So that you may be proved right when you speak, and win when you are judged."
But if our wrongdoing shows how right God is, what shall we say? That God is unfair to bring his anger on us? (I am using a human way of speaking.)
Certainly not! If that were so, how could God judge the world?
Someone might say, "If my lie makes God's truth stand out more and brings him glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?"
Why not say, as some people slanderously claim that we say, "Let us do evil so that good may come"? Their condemnation is deserved.
What then? Are we Jews any better? Not at all! We have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under the power of sin.
As the Scriptures say, "There is no one who is right with God, not even one.
There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks God.
All have turned away. Together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good, not even one."
"Their throats are open graves. Their tongues practise deceit." "The poison of snakes is under their lips."
"Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness."
"Their feet are quick to shed blood.
Ruin and misery mark their ways,
and the way of peace they have not known."
"There is no fear of God before their eyes."
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
So no one will be declared right in God's sight by doing what the law commands. Through the law we become aware of our sin.
But now God has shown a way to be right with him that does not depend on the law. The Law and the Prophets testify to it.
God makes people right with himself through faith in Jesus Christ. This is for everyone who believes. There is no difference.
For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
They are made right with him freely by his grace, through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.

God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of his blood, to be received by faith. He did this to show his justice, because in his patience he had left the sins committed beforehand unpunished.
He did it to show his justice at the present time, so as to be just and the one who makes right those who have faith in Jesus.
Where, then, is boasting? It is shut out. On what principle? On the principle of works? No, on the principle of faith.
For we maintain that a person is made right with God by faith, apart from doing what the law commands.
Is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of the nations also? Yes, of the nations also,
since there is only one God. He will make the circumcised right with himself by faith, and the uncircumcised right through that same faith.
Do we then cancel the law by this faith? Not at all! Rather, we uphold the law.
